boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Haverford College
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe food and essentials stops with directly documented evening hours on campus and along the nearby Main Line.

cards.title: Late Night Fare at the DC
cards.subtitle: The on-campus option for a meal before 10 p.m.
cards.notes: Go Monday through Thursday between 8 and 10 p.m. for the Dining Center’s explicitly scheduled Late Night Fare service.
cards.short_summary: Haverford’s own dining hall provides the board’s closest documented late-evening meal period.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford College lists Late Night Fare at the Dining Center from 8:00–10:00 p.m. Monday through Thursday.
cards.source_title: Dining Center | Dining Services | Haverford College
cards.access_notes: Late Night Fare is currently listed Monday–Thursday, 8:00–10:00 p.m.; academic breaks and special schedules may differ.

cards.title: Pizza Until 2 in Ardmore
cards.subtitle: A weekend carryout or delivery run on Greenfield Avenue
cards.notes: Use the Ardmore location for a Friday or Saturday pizza order; its official page lists both carryout and delivery until 2 a.m.
cards.short_summary: This Ardmore storefront extends a conventional pizza run well past midnight on weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: Papa Johns lists delivery and carryout at 24 Greenfield Avenue until 2:00 a.m. Friday and Saturday and midnight Sunday through Thursday.
cards.source_title: Papa Johns Greenfield Ave | Papa Johns Ardmore, PA
cards.access_notes: Carryout and delivery run until 2:00 a.m. Friday–Saturday and 12:00 a.m. Sunday–Thursday, according to the location page.

cards.title: The Rittenhouse Place Pizza Run
cards.subtitle: A midnight-or-later option in downtown Ardmore
cards.notes: Head to Rittenhouse Place when the timing calls for pizza late; the restaurant’s hosted menu documents service past midnight on weekends.
cards.short_summary: A downtown Ardmore pizzeria supplies a straightforward late pickup or delivery destination.
cards.evidence_claim: Ardmore Pizza’s directly hosted menu lists hours until midnight Sunday through Thursday and 1:00 a.m. Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: The hosted menu lists 11:00 a.m.–midnight Sunday–Thursday and 11:00 a.m.–1:00 a.m. Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: A Villanova-Side Pizza Run
cards.subtitle: Pizza, sandwiches, snacks, and shakes on Lancaster Avenue
cards.notes: Check the posted schedule before traveling to Villanova; the restaurant documents service through 11 p.m. or midnight on listed nights.
cards.short_summary: This student-oriented counter broadens a late run beyond pizza with sandwiches, snacks, breakfast food, and ice cream.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Corner Pizza’s official site lists 11:00 p.m. closing Monday and Thursday and midnight closing Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours are Monday and Thursday until 11:00 p.m. and Friday–Saturday until midnight; the site warns summer hours vary.

cards.title: An Ardmore Slice Before 11
cards.subtitle: A Lancaster Avenue pizza counter for Friday or Saturday
cards.notes: Plan this run for Friday or Saturday, when Bella Italia’s own site gives you an extra hour beyond its 10 p.m. weekday closing.
cards.short_summary: A long-running Ardmore pizza shop offers a clearly documented 11 p.m. weekend endpoint.
cards.evidence_claim: Bella Italia Pizza lists Friday and Saturday hours from 10:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. at 12 East Lancaster Avenue.
cards.source_title: Home | Bella Italia Pizza Ardmore, PA
cards.access_notes: Open until 11:00 p.m. Friday–Saturday; the official site lists 10:00 p.m. closing Monday–Thursday and Sunday.

cards.title: A Late Seated Dinner in Bryn Mawr
cards.subtitle: A BYOB Italian dining room with an 11 p.m. weekend kitchen
cards.notes: Reserve or arrive before the 10:30 p.m. last seating on Friday or Saturday; the kitchen’s published closing time is 11 p.m.
cards.short_summary: This Bryn Mawr restaurant fits a planned late dinner rather than a quick counter-service run.
cards.evidence_claim: Otto by Polpo lists a 10:30 p.m. last seating and 11:00 p.m. kitchen closing on Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Friday–Saturday last seating is 10:30 p.m., with the kitchen closing at 11:00 p.m.; Sunday–Thursday kitchen closes at 10:00 p.m.

cards.title: Bryn Mawr Dinner Through 10
cards.subtitle: A Friday or Saturday Italian dinner on Lancaster Avenue
cards.notes: Use this as a sit-down weekend run and place any takeout order early enough for the official 10 p.m. Friday–Saturday cutoff.
cards.short_summary: The restaurant’s direct ordering page documents a later weekend dinner window and a full savory menu.
cards.evidence_claim: Carina Sorella’s direct Toast ordering page lists Friday and Saturday ordering hours through 10:00 p.m.
cards.access_notes: The direct ordering page lists Friday–Saturday service from 4:00–10:00 p.m.; other evenings end between 9:15 and 9:30 p.m.

cards.title: A Saturday Carryout in Bryn Mawr
cards.subtitle: Pizza and hot-food pickup near Bryn Mawr Hospital
cards.notes: Choose Saturday carryout for the latest window; Lovecchio’s lists pickup until 9:45 p.m., later than its dining and delivery schedule.
cards.short_summary: This Bryn Mawr pizzeria provides a documented late pickup window for pizza, wings, fries, and sandwiches.
cards.evidence_claim: Lovecchio’s official website lists Saturday carryout from 10:00 a.m. until 9:45 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Saturday carryout is listed until 9:45 p.m.; most dining and delivery periods end at 8:45 p.m. or earlier.

cards.title: The 10 p.m. Essentials Run
cards.subtitle: Snacks and everyday supplies in Ardmore
cards.notes: Use the retail store for packaged snacks or forgotten essentials before 10 p.m.; pharmacy service ends earlier and should be checked separately.
cards.short_summary: This Ardmore CVS covers the practical version of a late run when the need is supplies rather than a prepared meal.
cards.evidence_claim: CVS lists its 317 West Lancaster Avenue store and photo department as open until 10:00 p.m.
cards.source_title: CVS Near Me | Ardmore, PA | CVS Pharmacy Locations
cards.access_notes: The retail store and photo counter are listed until 10:00 p.m.; the pharmacy closes earlier, currently at 8:00 p.m.

cards.title: A Havertown Supply Stop Before 10
cards.subtitle: Another late retail option for snacks and essentials
cards.notes: Go for retail items before the 10 p.m. store closing, but do not rely on that time for prescriptions because the pharmacy closes earlier.
cards.short_summary: The West Chester Pike store adds a distinct late-evening essentials option southwest of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: CVS lists the store and photo department at 1109 West Chester Pike in Havertown as open until 10:00 p.m.
cards.source_title: CVS Near Me | Havertown, PA | CVS Pharmacy Locations
cards.access_notes: The retail store and photo counter are listed until 10:00 p.m.; pharmacy service currently ends at 8:00 p.m.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: A practical field guide to Haverford’s reservable study rooms, creative workspaces, lounges, gathering areas, and student-run growing space.

cards.title: Bring the Group Project to Lutnick
cards.subtitle: Reservable collaboration rooms inside Allison and Howard Lutnick Library
cards.notes: Reserve through the College room system, then choose a room size that fits your group and the display or conferencing equipment you need.
cards.short_summary: Nine rooms provide purpose-built settings for small discussions, six-person collaborations, or larger meetings.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford Libraries lists six small, two medium, and one large group study room in Lutnick Library, with shared displays and collaboration equipment.
cards.access_notes: Group study rooms are reservable through the College room reservation system; follow the reservation holder’s assigned time.

cards.entity_name: White Science Library Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Work It Out on a Whiteboard
cards.subtitle: Four shared study rooms on the third floor of KINSC-Hilles
cards.notes: Use a medium room when the group needs ten seats and a large monitor; select a small room for a four-person chalkboard or whiteboard session.
cards.short_summary: Science Library rooms pair writable surfaces with configurations sized for four or ten people.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford Libraries documents two ten-seat medium rooms with whiteboards and monitors and two four-seat small rooms with whiteboards or chalkboards.
cards.access_notes: Rooms are in the White Science Library on KINSC-Hilles’s third floor and are reservable through the College room system.

cards.title: Prototype With People Nearby
cards.subtitle: A supervised fabrication and craft lab in VCAM Room 005
cards.notes: Visit during posted Open Studio hours, sign in, and ask a student worker which tools require training before beginning a fabrication project.
cards.short_summary: The lab supports collaborative digital fabrication, craft, prototyping, and cross-disciplinary experimentation.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Maker Arts Space page says the lab serves students through coursework, workshops, and studio hours and documents students collaborating there.
cards.source_title: Maker Arts Space | Visual Culture, Arts, and Media VCAM
cards.access_notes: Academic-year Open Studio hours are posted on the source page. Walk-ins are welcome, but machine-specific training and material restrictions apply.

cards.entity_name: VCAM Presentation Lounge and Community Kitchen
cards.title: Gather at VCAM’s Shared Center
cards.subtitle: A central lounge and community kitchen anchoring VCAM’s creative rooms
cards.notes: Use the lounge as a meeting point before a screening, workshop, or exhibition, and check program requirements before planning kitchen activity.
cards.short_summary: This central pair of spaces connects VCAM’s teaching, production, exhibition, and making facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford’s official VCAM description identifies a central Presentation Lounge and Community Kitchen as the anchor for the facility’s flexible spaces.
cards.source_title: About | Visual Culture, Arts, and Media VCAM
cards.access_notes: VCAM is described as a 24/7 creative hub, but individual rooms may be scheduled for teaching, projects, or events; observe posted restrictions.

cards.title: Join a Working Campus Farm
cards.subtitle: A year-round educational growing space near the greenhouse
cards.notes: Look for a scheduled student activity or workshop before heading over, then arrive ready to learn how the farm connects food, agriculture, and community.
cards.short_summary: The farm links hands-on growing with food justice, coursework, extracurricular learning, and community distribution.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford describes Haverfarm as a year-round farming and educational space integrated into students’ academic and extracurricular lives.
cards.access_notes: Participate through announced farm activities or workshops and follow staff guidance around active beds, tools, and greenhouse areas.

cards.title: Head Below the Dining Center to Study
cards.subtitle: A large open work area beside student organization spaces
cards.notes: Try the basement when you need an open study setting near club and affinity-group offices, while yielding to any scheduled gathering or performance.
cards.short_summary: The Dining Center’s lower level combines an open study area with student organizations and a black-box theater.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford’s campus map description states that the Dining Center basement contains affinity-group offices, club spaces, and a large open study area.
cards.access_notes: The study area shares a level with organization offices and performance space; respect scheduled uses and any posted building-access rules.

cards.title: Settle Into the Sunken Lounge
cards.subtitle: The Dining Center’s shared lounge, with a seasonal fireplace
cards.notes: Use the lounge for a conversation or pause between commitments, and keep circulation clear when the Dining Center is hosting a larger event.
cards.short_summary: This lounge gives the Dining Center a gathering area separate from its meal-service seating.
cards.evidence_claim: The official campus map says the Dining Center opens into a Sunken Lounge, where a fire often burns in colder months, and hosts larger gatherings and events.
cards.access_notes: Access follows Dining Center building hours and event arrangements; food service may require a meal plan or purchase, but lounge use is distinct.

cards.title: Meet in the Union Building Lounge
cards.subtitle: A student lounge inside an interdisciplinary academic building
cards.notes: Use the lounge for a small meetup around classes in Union, keeping noise appropriate for the classrooms and academic offices elsewhere in the building.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated lounge adds informal student space to Union’s classrooms and interdisciplinary programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford’s campus map states that Union Building includes classrooms, a student lounge, and a listening room.
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to normal academic-building access and any room reservations or posted program restrictions.

cards.title: Use the Lounge Built Into the Floor
cards.subtitle: Residential study space shared by Tritton Hall neighbors
cards.notes: For residents and their invited guests, use the floor lounge for collaborative work while following quiet hours and keeping the common area available to others.
cards.short_summary: Each residential floor pairs two common areas with a dedicated study lounge.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford’s campus map says Tritton Hall provides two common areas and one study lounge on every floor.
cards.access_notes: Tritton is a residence hall; access is for residents and authorized guests under current Residential Life policies.

cards.title: Combine Errands, Art, and a Meetup
cards.subtitle: A campus center containing the Coop, bookstore, and Cantor Fitzgerald Gallery
cards.notes: Coordinate a meetup around the gallery or campus errands, and check each destination’s current hours because services inside operate independently.
cards.short_summary: Whitehead brings student-facing services, a café, retail, and an exhibition venue into one recognizable stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford’s official campus map says Whitehead Campus Center contains the Coop, Bookstore, Cantor Fitzgerald Gallery, Admission, and Financial Aid.
cards.access_notes: Public restrooms are available on the ground floor during normal business hours; individual services and the gallery maintain their own access schedules.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten named Arboretum stops for a no-purchase outdoor meet-up, using the College’s public free-tour and collection-access policy.

cards.title: Walk the Nature Trail
cards.subtitle: Haverford College Arboretum
cards.notes: Meet at the trailhead and walk a section together; keep bikes off the trail and coordinate with the Arboretum before bringing a planned large group.
cards.short_summary: A 2.2-mile campus-perimeter walk with woods, meadows, and pond views.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford’s Living Collections Policy says the Arboretum provides open and reasonable access and offers free campus tours to the public; the Nature Trail is a named Arboretum route.
cards.access_notes: Use the trail as a self-guided visit; large planned groups must contact the Arboretum first. The College policy describes free public campus tours and open collection access.

cards.title: Watch for Wildlife at Duck Pond
cards.subtitle: Haverford College Arboretum
cards.notes: Bring a friend, pause at the pond edge, and look quietly for birds, fish, turtles, and frogs without feeding or disturbing wildlife.
cards.short_summary: A three-acre campus pond and a natural observation stop.
cards.evidence_claim: The Duck Pond is a named Haverford Arboretum highlight; the College’s Living Collections Policy provides open and reasonable access and states that free campus tours are regularly offered to the public.
cards.access_notes: Stay on appropriate paths and do not feed waterfowl. The College policy describes free public campus tours and open collection access.

cards.title: Meet Beneath the Treaty Elm
cards.subtitle: Barclay Beach, Haverford College Arboretum
cards.notes: Use the lawn by Barclay Hall as a conversation stop, then read the Arboretum history for the remaining elm from the 1915 planting.
cards.short_summary: A named historic elm on the Barclay Beach lawn.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford identifies the Treaty Elm as the remaining tree from seven American elm grafts planted behind Barclay Hall; its Arboretum policy provides open access and free public campus tours.
cards.access_notes: Visit as part of an outdoor Arboretum walk; do not climb trees. The College policy describes free public campus tours and open collection access.

cards.title: Read Tree Labels in the Ryan Pinetum
cards.subtitle: Haverford College Arboretum
cards.notes: Walk together through the conifer collection and compare the labels; the Pinetum’s tree labels include botanical names and family names.
cards.short_summary: An 18-acre conifer collection for a slow, label-led walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford identifies the Ryan Pinetum as a named Arboretum collection and documents its tree-label system; the policy provides open access and free public campus tours.
cards.source_title: State Champion Trees | Arboretum | Haverford College
cards.access_notes: Remain on appropriate paths and leave plant material in place. The College policy describes free public campus tours and open collection access.

cards.title: Look for the Asian Gardens’ Artifacts
cards.subtitle: Beside the Dining Center, Haverford College Arboretum
cards.notes: Take a short outdoor loop beside the Dining Center and identify the garden features together; enjoy the setting without entering dining facilities.
cards.short_summary: Two named gardens with landscape design and donated artifacts.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford identifies the Gertrude C. Teaf Garden and Denis Asian Garden as its Asian Gardens; the Arboretum policy provides open access and free public campus tours.
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor garden visit beside the Dining Center. The College policy describes free public campus tours and open collection access.

cards.title: Visit Haverfarm’s Outdoor Growing Area
cards.subtitle: Haverford College Arboretum
cards.notes: Meet by the farm signage and discuss what is growing; observe the educational farm space without harvesting produce or entering work areas.
cards.short_summary: A named year-round farm and educational space on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford describes Haverfarm as a year-round farming and educational space for students, faculty, staff, and community members; the Arboretum policy provides open access and free public campus tours.
cards.source_title: Sustainable Haverford | Haverford College Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Observe from public outdoor areas and do not harvest. The College policy describes free public campus tours and open collection access.

cards.entity_name: Penn State Certified Pollinator Garden Walk
cards.title: Trace the Pollinator Garden
cards.subtitle: Adjacent to Duck Pond, Haverford College Arboretum
cards.notes: Walk the garden edge with friends and look for insects and flowering plants; keep clear of planted areas and leave all plants and wildlife undisturbed.
cards.short_summary: A named 10-acre certified pollinator garden beside Duck Pond.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford’s campus map identifies a Penn State Certified Pollinator Garden adjacent to Duck Pond; the Arboretum policy provides open access and free public campus tours.
cards.source_title: Sustainable Haverford | Haverford College Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Stay on paths around planted areas. The College policy describes free public campus tours and open collection access.

cards.title: Inspect the VCAM Rain Garden
cards.subtitle: Visual Culture, Arts, and Media building, Haverford College
cards.notes: Meet outside VCAM and follow the rain garden’s planted edge, comparing how its landscaping relates to the building’s runoff-management purpose.
cards.short_summary: A named rain garden outside the VCAM building.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford’s campus map identifies a rain garden outside the Visual Culture, Arts, and Media building; the Arboretum policy provides open access and free public campus tours.
cards.source_title: Sustainable Haverford | Haverford College Campus Map
cards.access_notes: View from public outdoor areas and avoid planted beds. The College policy describes free public campus tours and open collection access.

cards.title: Pause at the Peace Garden
cards.subtitle: Haverford College Arboretum
cards.notes: Make this a quiet outdoor conversation stop, then continue the campus walk; respect the garden beds and leave any plants, flowers, and seeds in place.
cards.short_summary: A named additional area of interest within Haverford’s Arboretum.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford lists the Peace Garden as an Arboretum area of interest; the College’s Living Collections Policy provides open and reasonable collection access and states that free campus tours are regularly offered to the public.
cards.access_notes: Use as an outdoor Arboretum stop; do not walk in flower beds or harvest plants. The College policy describes free public campus tours and open collection access.

cards.title: Take a Hilles Garden Loop
cards.subtitle: Haverford College Arboretum
cards.notes: Add the garden to a short campus loop and compare seasonal planting as you walk; keep to accessible paths and treat the beds as display areas.
cards.short_summary: A named additional garden area within the Haverford Arboretum.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford lists Hilles Garden as an Arboretum area of interest; the College’s Living Collections Policy provides open and reasonable collection access and states that free campus tours are regularly offered to the public.
cards.access_notes: Use public outdoor paths and do not enter flower beds. The College policy describes free public campus tours and open collection access.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented Haverford study settings, from heritage reading rooms to reservable collaboration spaces, with current access and room-use details.

cards.entity_name: Nan and Bill Harris Digital Scholarship Commons
cards.title: Spread Out in the Digital Commons
cards.subtitle: Flexible, technology-rich study on Lutnick Library’s second level
cards.notes: Bring a collaborative or digital project; use the flexible seating, Google Jamboards, and nearby technology-rich group rooms.
cards.short_summary: A flexible workspace designed for technology-assisted scholarship and collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford identifies this level-two Lutnick space as featuring flexible seating, Google Jamboards, and technology-rich group study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Located on level 2 of Lutnick Library; consult the current library-hours page before visiting.

cards.title: Put the Full Team Around One Table
cards.subtitle: A 14-seat group room with presentation and conferencing equipment
cards.notes: Reserve this room for a large working session, then connect to the 85-inch display or integrated web-conferencing system.
cards.short_summary: The largest documented Lutnick group-study room supports presentations and remote participants.
cards.evidence_claim: Room 202 has a 14-seat rectangular table, an 85-inch display, a Mersive POD, professional audio, Listen Assist, and a PTZ webcam.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through the College room-reservation system; access is subject to Lutnick Library hours.

cards.title: Workshop a Draft in Room 129
cards.subtitle: A medium group room for six, with capacity for two more
cards.notes: Book Room 129 for a discussion or rehearsal; its table box, webcam, display, and Listen Assist support shared work.
cards.short_summary: A reservable medium room sized for a seminar-style study session.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford describes Room 129 as a medium group-study room with a rectangular table, six chairs, a 65-inch display, webcam, Mersive POD, and Listen Assist.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through the College room-reservation system; the stated configuration seats six and can accommodate two more.

cards.title: Gather Four Around the Round Table
cards.subtitle: A compact group room with a 55-inch display
cards.notes: Reserve Room 126 for a four-person problem set or edit session, and use the display wallplate and Mersive POD to share work.
cards.short_summary: A compact reservable room with an equal-footing round-table layout.
cards.evidence_claim: Room 126 is one of Lutnick’s approximately 13-by-10-foot small group rooms, furnished with a round table, four chairs, a 55-inch display, wallplate, and Mersive POD.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through the College room-reservation system; access is subject to Lutnick Library hours.

cards.title: Map the Problem on a Whiteboard
cards.subtitle: A ten-seat science-library collaboration room
cards.notes: Reserve Room 305B when the work needs diagrams or shared calculations; the whiteboard and large monitor suit visible thinking.
cards.short_summary: A medium group room pairing ten seats with analog and digital work surfaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford lists White Science Library Room 305B as a medium group-study room with a whiteboard, large flat-screen monitor, and seating for ten.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through the College room-reservation system; White Science Library is on the third floor of KINSC-Hilles.

cards.title: Take a Four-Person Science Huddle
cards.subtitle: A small room with a board for working through ideas
cards.notes: Choose Room 304C for a focused four-person session; reserve ahead and use the room’s board to keep calculations visible.
cards.short_summary: A small reservable science-library room built around face-to-face work.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford lists White Science Library Room 304C among its four-seat small group rooms, equipped with a whiteboard or chalkboard.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through the College room-reservation system; White Science Library is on the third floor of KINSC-Hilles.

cards.title: Reserve Two Hours of Solo Focus
cards.subtitle: Individual carrels with a clear reservation priority
cards.notes: Claim a two-hour block through EMS or a nearby kiosk; without a booking, use an open carrel but yield to its reservation holder.
cards.short_summary: A structured solo-work option with short bookings and semester access for thesis writers.
cards.evidence_claim: Lutnick carrels can be reserved for two-hour blocks, while another block is available to thesis writers for semester-long reservations.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through EMS or the carrel-area kiosk. Unreserved use is allowed, but occupants must yield to reservation holders.

cards.title: Read Beneath the Vaulted Ceiling
cards.subtitle: A heritage reading environment inside Lutnick Library
cards.notes: Settle into the Philips Wing for reading-oriented work, and consult the building map first to distinguish its tiers and entrances.
cards.short_summary: A named historic wing offering a visually distinctive library setting.
cards.evidence_claim: The Libraries’ Places & Hours page identifies the Philips Wing with a photograph of its vaulted ceilings, and the official building map labels the wing across multiple tiers.
cards.access_notes: Inside Lutnick Library and available subject to current building hours; no separate reservation rule is stated on the source page.

cards.title: Find the Rufus Jones Study
cards.subtitle: A named heritage room in Lutnick Library’s Philips Wing
cards.notes: Use the official floor map to locate this tucked-away named room, then confirm availability on arrival because no booking policy is posted.
cards.short_summary: A map-documented heritage room within the older portion of Lutnick Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford’s official Lutnick Library floor map labels the Rufus Jones Study within the Philips Wing.
cards.source_title: Haverford College Magill Library Floor Maps
cards.access_notes: Located inside Lutnick Library. The official map confirms the room, but the College does not publish a separate reservation rule for it.

cards.title: Work Directly with the Archives
cards.subtitle: A supervised research room for collection-based study
cards.notes: Bring a laptop, tablet, phone, camera, pencil, or paper; register daily, store other belongings in a locker, and keep food and water outside.
cards.short_summary: A public research setting reserved for hands-on work with special-collections materials.
cards.evidence_claim: The Reading Room welcomes researchers without an affiliation or ID requirement, but is reserved for people using Quaker & Special Collections materials under posted handling rules.
cards.source_title: Accessing Materials & Reproductions | Haverford College Libraries
cards.access_notes: Appointments are not required. Register and sign in each day; the room is only for researchers using collection materials.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations in the Lancaster Avenue corridor at Suburban Square in nearby Ardmore, each with one source-backed reason to stop.

cards.title: Ardmore Farmers Market
cards.subtitle: Lancaster Avenue corridor, Suburban Square
cards.notes: Walk the market’s vendor aisles and choose from produce, prepared meals, meats, seafood, and sweets; check the posted market hours before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A seven-day indoor market with a broad mix of food vendors.
cards.evidence_claim: The official market page says it is open seven days a week and lists vendors offering prepared meals, produce, meats, seafood, sweet treats, and more.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: Monday–Saturday 8 a.m.–6 p.m.; Sunday 9 a.m.–4 p.m.

cards.title: Ardmore Produce
cards.subtitle: Lancaster Avenue corridor, inside Ardmore Farmers Market
cards.notes: Browse the produce displays, then use the made-to-order juice bar if you want a drink prepared on site; purchases are separate from market entry.
cards.short_summary: A market produce stand that also lists a made-to-order juice bar.
cards.evidence_claim: Suburban Square identifies Ardmore Produce as a local business in the market and says it has produce plus a made-to-order fruit-and-vegetable juice bar.
cards.access_notes: Located within Ardmore Farmers Market at Suburban Square; consult the market page for current building hours.

cards.title: The Buttery
cards.subtitle: Lancaster Avenue corridor, inside Ardmore Farmers Market
cards.notes: Use this market counter for coffee, pastries, breads, soups, salads, or sandwiches when you want a compact food stop along the corridor.
cards.short_summary: A market counter listing coffee, baked goods, and savory lunch items.
cards.evidence_claim: The Suburban Square dining directory lists The Buttery in Ardmore Farmers Market and describes its coffee, pastries, breads, soups, salads, and sandwiches.
cards.access_notes: Located within Ardmore Farmers Market at Suburban Square; consult the market page for current building hours.

cards.title: Tabouli
cards.subtitle: Lancaster Avenue corridor, inside Ardmore Farmers Market
cards.notes: Pick this counter when you want Mediterranean food prepared fresh daily with whole-food ingredients; its official listing places it inside the market.
cards.short_summary: A Mediterranean-food counter in the Ardmore Farmers Market.
cards.evidence_claim: The Suburban Square dining directory describes Tabouli as Mediterranean cuisine prepared fresh daily with whole-food ingredients and locates it in Ardmore Farmers Market.
cards.access_notes: Located within Ardmore Farmers Market at Suburban Square; consult the market page for current building hours.

cards.title: CAVA
cards.subtitle: Lancaster Avenue corridor, Suburban Square
cards.notes: Build a greens-and-grains bowl, salad, or pita at this fast-casual stop; the official center directory lists all three menu formats.
cards.short_summary: A fast-casual Mediterranean option for customizable bowls, salads, and pitas.
cards.evidence_claim: Suburban Square’s dining directory describes CAVA as a fast-casual Mediterranean restaurant serving customizable greens-and-grains bowls, salads, and pitas.
cards.access_notes: At Suburban Square, whose posted general hours are Monday–Saturday 10 a.m.–8 p.m. and Sunday noon–5 p.m.; merchant hours may differ.

cards.title: Urban Outfitters
cards.subtitle: Lancaster Avenue corridor, 40 Coulter Avenue
cards.notes: Browse apparel, accessories, and home items at the Coulter Avenue storefront; its center listing supplies the exact Suburban Square address.
cards.short_summary: A retail storefront with apparel, accessories, and home merchandise.
cards.evidence_claim: The Suburban Square store page places Urban Outfitters at 40 Coulter Avenue and describes its mix of women’s, men’s, accessories, and home assortments.
cards.access_notes: At 40 Coulter Avenue, Ardmore; verify store hours directly before a visit.

cards.title: Warby Parker
cards.subtitle: Lancaster Avenue corridor, Suburban Square
cards.notes: Stop in to browse the current eyewear line or arrange an eye exam; the center directory specifically identifies both services at this location.
cards.short_summary: An eyewear shop whose directory entry also mentions eye exams.
cards.evidence_claim: Suburban Square’s shopping directory says visitors can explore Warby Parker’s eyewear line and get an eye exam at the location.
cards.access_notes: At Suburban Square; verify appointment availability and store hours directly before a visit.

cards.title: Paper Source
cards.subtitle: Lancaster Avenue corridor, Suburban Square
cards.notes: Use this named shop for stationery, paper goods, and a visually focused retail stop while moving between Lancaster Avenue and Coulter Avenue.
cards.short_summary: A named paper-goods shop listed in the Suburban Square directory.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Suburban Square shopping directory lists Paper Source as a current shop at the center.
cards.access_notes: At Suburban Square; posted center hours are Monday–Saturday 10 a.m.–8 p.m. and Sunday noon–5 p.m., with merchant hours varying.

cards.title: Apple
cards.subtitle: Lancaster Avenue corridor, Suburban Square
cards.notes: Visit the Apple storefront for a clearly named technology-retail destination in the center; confirm service or shopping needs with the store before traveling.
cards.short_summary: An Apple retail location listed in the Suburban Square shopping directory.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Suburban Square shopping directory lists Apple Computer as a current shop at the center.
cards.access_notes: At Suburban Square; posted center hours are Monday–Saturday 10 a.m.–8 p.m. and Sunday noon–5 p.m., with merchant hours varying.

cards.title: Axiom Contemporary
cards.subtitle: Lancaster Avenue corridor, Suburban Square
cards.notes: Look for the gallery’s contemporary-art presentation while exploring the shopping corridor; the center directory identifies it as featuring work by emerging artists.
cards.short_summary: A contemporary-art gallery listed at Suburban Square.
cards.evidence_claim: Suburban Square’s shopping directory lists Axiom Contemporary and describes it as contemporary art from emerging artists.
cards.access_notes: At Suburban Square; confirm gallery hours and entry details directly before a visit.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Haverford College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A calm, campus-centered sequence of places to orient yourself, eat, make, browse, and catch a public program.

cards.entity_name: Giancarlo and Maria Cristina Galdi Integrated Academic Center
cards.title: Start at the GIAC Lobby
cards.subtitle: Arrival and campus orientation
cards.notes: Use the GIAC Lobby as a recognizable first anchor, then open the College’s interactive map and identify the paths to your next few stops.
cards.short_summary: Begin with a named campus landmark and map reference.
cards.evidence_claim: The College identifies the GIAC Lobby as the location for new-student check-in and links its campus map from arrival information.
cards.access_notes: Check the College’s arrival and campus-map information for current access details.

cards.title: Pause at Founders Hall
cards.subtitle: A historic campus landmark
cards.notes: Walk to Founders Hall and take in the building’s central place on campus; save its Great Hall programming for an event that is actually posted.
cards.short_summary: Connect the weekend route to Haverford’s original college building.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford states that Founders Hall was built in 1833, originally housed the entire college, and includes Founders Great Hall for events.
cards.access_notes: Administrative and event spaces may have limited access; view current event listings before entering program areas.

cards.title: Find the original swamp white oak
cards.subtitle: Lloyd Green, between Founders Hall and Marshall Auditorium
cards.notes: Make this one tree your arboretum introduction: locate it on Lloyd Green, observe its canopy, and use the Arboretum Explorer for more labeled specimens.
cards.short_summary: A specific living landmark from the original landscape plan.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arboretum identifies an original swamp white oak on Lloyd Green between Founders Hall and Marshall Auditorium.
cards.source_title: Haverford College's Original Oaks | Haverford College
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; follow posted campus and landscape guidance.

cards.title: Walk down to Duck Pond
cards.subtitle: Arboretum highlight
cards.notes: Continue downhill for a short outdoor reset at Duck Pond, then look toward Roberts Hall and the surrounding meadow before moving on.
cards.short_summary: A named pond with a documented student-and-community history.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford documents Duck Pond as a year-round campus feature used by students and the community, with the historic skate house still present.
cards.access_notes: Stay on maintained paths and observe posted pond-area guidance.

cards.title: Take a section of the Nature Trail
cards.subtitle: Arboretum perimeter route
cards.notes: Choose a daylight section rather than attempting the full route; the trail passes conifers, meadows, fields, woodlands, and the campus ponds.
cards.short_summary: A flexible walking leg through the College Arboretum.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford says its 2.2-mile Nature Trail roughly follows the campus perimeter and passes through arboretum collections, meadows, fields, woodlands, and ponds.
cards.access_notes: Use during daylight and follow posted conditions; trail surfaces and maintenance can vary.

cards.title: Plan a weekend meal at the Dining Center
cards.subtitle: Campus dining
cards.notes: Check the current menu and hours before heading over; Saturday service is listed for breakfast, brunch, light lunch, and dinner.
cards.short_summary: A practical food stop with officially published weekend service.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford’s Dining Center page lists Saturday breakfast, brunch, light lunch, and dinner service.
cards.source_title: Dining Center | Haverford College Dining Services
cards.access_notes: Hours and meal service can change; consult the Dining Center page or posted updates before visiting.

cards.title: Settle into Lutnick Library
cards.subtitle: Library study and research spaces
cards.notes: Use this stop to get familiar with the main library’s study options, service points, café, and reservable rooms before coursework gets busy.
cards.short_summary: A named library with study, technology, and research support.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford lists study rooms, reservable carrels, computers, scanners, a café, and research support at Lutnick Library.
cards.access_notes: Current building and visitor hours are published by the Libraries; some rooms require reservations.

cards.title: Browse the Cantor Fitzgerald Gallery
cards.subtitle: Whitehead Campus Center, first floor
cards.notes: See what exhibition is currently installed, then use the gallery’s directions page to navigate from the Campus Center entrance or elevator.
cards.short_summary: A campus exhibition stop with published weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The gallery’s official directions page places it on the first floor of Whitehead Campus Center and lists Saturday–Sunday hours of noon–5 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Officially listed weekend hours are noon–5 p.m.; confirm the current exhibition and any closures before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Visual Culture, Arts, and Media Building
cards.title: Look into VCAM programming
cards.subtitle: Visual Culture, Arts, and Media
cards.notes: Stop by the VCAM Building and check its public programs or exhibitions; ask staff about workshops and maker opportunities that fit your interests.
cards.short_summary: A creative hub for visual studies, arts, media, and making.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford describes VCAM as a creative hub housing visual studies, maker arts, the Hurford Center, and the Haverford Innovations Program.
cards.source_title: Visual Culture, Arts, and Media VCAM | Haverford College
cards.access_notes: The College describes VCAM as a 24/7 hub, but individual studios, equipment, and programs can have eligibility or scheduling requirements.

cards.title: End with a Roberts Hall program
cards.subtitle: Music and performance venue
cards.notes: Check the Department of Music calendar and choose a posted concert or talk in Roberts Hall; arrive for the actual listed start time.
cards.short_summary: A final event-oriented stop anchored by campus performance spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford states that public concerts are held in Michael Jaharis Recital Hall and Marshall Auditorium in Roberts Hall.
cards.access_notes: Attend only events listed on the College calendar; ticketing, start times, and access vary by program.
